problems.claim: Every positive-density GCD graph either has the stated degree bound at every vertex or has a same-data subgraph of strictly greater quality.
problems.location: Definition1 p13, Definition2 pp13–14, Lemma10.1 pp22–23, Lemma8.6 p23
problems.parameters: tau=1/200; mu(1)=1, mu(n)=0 otherwise; V={1,2}, W={1}, E={(1,1)}, P empty
problems.check: mu(V)=mu(W)=mu(E)=delta=q=1. Vertex2 has empty neighborhood, violating 0>=201/401. Every same-data subgraph has quality0 or1, so no strict increase is possible.
problems.suspect_step: Strict low-degree inequality multiplied by zero mass on p23.
problems.counterevidence: Strict increment valid on positive support; no hidden positivity in rendered Definition1. Whole high-degree subgraph existence remains repairable with unchanged weighted quantities.
problems.impact: Local false auxiliary dichotomy; no demonstrated failure of bilinear estimates or main theorems.

correction.statement: Restrict Lemma10.1 to positive-weight vertices; for unrestricted Lemma8.6 delete zero-weight vertices first, then maximize quality.
correction.verification: All deleted edge product masses are zero, so totals/density/quality unchanged; GCD conditions inherited. For positive vertex mass, logarithmic derivative of (1-cx)^(2+tau)/(1-x)^(1+tau) is positive, establishing strict gain.

independent_acceptance_review.summary: P1 is an admissible zero-weight counterexample to the literal Lemma10.1 dichotomy. Restricting to positive support preserves all graph masses, density, multiplicative data and quality, and restores the high-degree existence conclusion used downstream. Minor is supported. The separate Section16 sharpness observation remains an explicitly scoped Needs Evidence inference, not an arithmetic counterexample.
